Background (from the session that started this one):
JusPrin (OrcaSlicer fork, C++17, wxWidgets) has an in-app Agent that sends the whole chat to a model provider (Anthropic Messages API or OpenAI Responses API, directly or through the JusPrin Cloud gateway) on every call. Today the host rebuilds earlier turns in a shorter form at each new turn, so provider prompt caches miss and about 70% of an Opus bill was cache writes. Kenneth (the owner) is running a measured, step-by-step programme to make the history byte-stable; the working plan is the untracked file `chat-history-cache-plan.md` in the main checkout `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin` (read it, and `chat-history-measurement.md` next to it, but never commit either). The integration branch is `claude/chat-history-cache` (commit `cd4162fa97`), which your worktree is cut from. A key finding (M1): no full live request body exists anywhere; the app has no request-body logging and the project-prompt recorder cut stored results at 4,000 characters. Every later step (an OpenAI baseline, live before/after cache runs, checking that consecutive requests share a byte-identical prefix) needs the bodies, not just token counts. Your piece is that logging. Constraints: no live model calls of any kind (Kenneth approves paid batches individually; this task needs none). Keep production code in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/` untouched unless a tiny additive seam is unavoidable; prefer a wrapping transport in test code. Commit on your branch only, no push, no merge, never stage submodules, no attribution lines in commit messages. Temp notes stay untracked in the worktree root. Shared Mac build rules: check `uptime` and `pgrep -fl ninja` first, pass `-- -j4`, one build per build directory, never restart a running build to change targets, run long builds with nohup and watch the log (a foreground Bash call that times out kills the build), and never end your turn to "wait for the build": block in the tool call until it finishes. Two sibling sessions work at the same time on `AgentHost.cpp` and on `ProviderAgent.cpp` plus the codecs, so add new tests at the end of test files and avoid editing those sources.

Task:
Add request-body logging to the shell harness so that every model request the Agent posts during a harness run is written to disk exactly as posted, one file per request, with the response's usage line beside it.

Where things are:
- The transport interface is `IAgentHttpTransport` in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/AgentTransport.hpp` (`post(AgentHttpRequest, EventFn)`); the Agent posts through it. The cleanest design is a logging transport in the harness that wraps whichever real or fake transport the harness builds, writes the body bytes before forwarding, and writes the usage/stop fields from the streamed response events after.
- The shell harness is `tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp`; `--live-agent` is handled around line 13150. Find how the live and fake transports are built and wrap them there.
- The project-prompt recorder (`tests/project_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py`, `requests.json`, its README) stores scripted bodies and cut stored results at 4,000 characters. Leave its format unchanged; the new log is a separate, uncut, byte-exact record.
- The Catch2 agent tests in `tests/agent/test_agent_bridge.cpp` show fake transports and streamed replies (`RecordingProvider`, `anthropic_stream`, `responses_stream`) you can reuse as models.

Deliverables:
1. A harness flag (for example `--request-log DIR`) that, when set, writes for each request `<n>-request.json` (bytes exactly as posted, plus a small sidecar or header with provider, endpoint, chat id and timestamp) and `<n>-response.json` (the usage and stop fields, and the final assembled response text if cheap to get). Numbering is per run, in post order. Works for both wire formats.
2. A Catch2 or harness test that drives a scripted (fake) run with the flag set and proves the file bytes equal what the transport posted, and that two requests give two files.
3. A small script `tests/project_prompt/prefix_check.py` that takes a log directory and, for consecutive requests of the same chat, reports the length of the common byte prefix, the first differing byte offset and the JSON path at which they diverge. This is the check phase 2 will use to find cache leaks. Give it a unit test on two tiny hand-written bodies.
4. A short section in `tests/shell/README.md` (or the harness's existing doc; find which one documents flags) on the flag and the script.

Done means: the agent suite and your new tests pass in your worktree's build; a scripted harness run with the flag produces files; nothing in `requests.json` or existing baselines changed; one or a few commits on your branch with messages that explain what and why; an untracked note `request-log-report.md` in the worktree root saying what you built, how you verified it, and anything you could not verify (there is no live run, say so).

Shared notes folder for this group of sessions (outside the repo; read siblings' notes there, leave hand-over notes or large findings there instead of pasting them into messages): /Users/kenneth/Library/Application Support/Claude/side-session-notes/local_34d95bfb-fc90-47e6-94ab-adc3d3711d01

Write prefix_check.py and its unit test
Add a test proving logged bytes match posted
Build and run tests and a scripted harness run
Document flag and script in README

# Chat history cache: plan and progress

Working doc, 2026-10-29. Keep it untracked: never commit it, never add it to `.gitignore`.
Companion to `chat-history-cache-handoff.md` (the archaeology of every decision) and
`chat-history-measurement.md` (M1's numbers).

## Goal

The in-app Agent should resend earlier turns to the model exactly as it sent them, so the
provider's prompt cache covers the whole conversation, not just the system prompt and tools.
Both Anthropic and OpenAI stay supported. Every past optimization that makes the history change
is either reverted (when the revert simplifies the code and removes a cache-miss scenario) or
kept only after a measurement shows it does something.

## Decisions Kenneth owns (all settled 2026-10-29)

| # | Decision | Proposal | What M1/M2 add | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | What the chat record holds | The exact request content as sent, per chat, thinking included (a chat is bound to one provider) | Thinking is part of the 3,500–9,000 tokens dropped at every turn start; Anthropic rejects edited history once thinking is carried (400 errors, accounts after 2026-08-31) | **decided 2026-10-29** (side session `local_97f342dd`): append-only record of every item ever sent, thinking included, pictures as blob references never inline base64. Visibility is a lifetime flag per item, never an edit of the record. See "Roles and lifetimes" below. |
| D2 | App notes in the project chat | Append where they happened, or never send them | A note is ~30 bytes. Not neutral: the guard test shows that without the note, two consecutive assistant replies merge into one message on Anthropic | **decided 2026-10-29**: notes become operator-role in-conversation messages (Anthropic in-array `role:"system"`, OpenAI `developer`), kept in the record, never cleared; one treatment for project and printer chat. Replaces the "JusPrin app note, not the person's words" user-text prefix. |
| D3 | Behaviour at the real context limit | Visible compaction that knowingly starts a new cache, or a refusal with a message. No rolling trim | The 64 KiB trim never fired in any recorded request (max replayed history ~27 KB); R3 is a plain deletion plus whatever D3 picks | **decided 2026-10-29**: visible compaction that knowingly starts a new cache. No rolling trim, no silent cut. The compaction is an item in the chat the person can see; the earlier items stay in the record with their lifetime cleared (fits D1), so it lands with R7, not before. |
| D4 | File-load "data, not instructions" reminder | Delete it; the standing prompt has said the same since 86f8395071; keep the injection eval case | 215 bytes at the very front; flips on every chat; the guard test fails at messages[0] because of it | **narrowed 2026-10-29**: either deleted (standing prompt already says it) or a turn-scoped operator message like a skill (cleared at the next user message on Anthropic, stays visible on OpenAI). **decided 2026-10-29: delete it.** Keep the injection eval case (live run, batched with the baselines). |
| D5 | Mid-chat model switching | Allowed within one wire format; a cross-format switch (Anthropic ↔ Responses, including JusPrin Cloud aliases served in different formats) starts a new chat or is hidden from the picker for an existing chat | Anthropic docs (preserved-thinking reference, as of 2026-09-03): a model switch never fails a request; blocks the new model cannot read are dropped unbilled, the stored history is never edited; the only cost is one cold cache, same as a thinking-level change. Cross-format is different: OpenAI reasoning items are encrypted and the record is in one provider's shape, so switching would mean re-rendering history, which D1 forbids | **decided 2026-10-29** (Kenneth, forked side session): keep same-format switching, no history edit on switch; R7 adds the cross-format check in `handle_set_chat_model` |
| D6 | Spend approval for phase 2 live batches | ~$1.20 per Opus run, far less per OpenAI run; two runs each (before/after) | | **approved 2026-10-29** for the phase 2 before/after batches on both providers; the OpenAI "before" run is M4. The prompt-case baseline and the injection eval case are extra batches: ask before running them. |
| D7 | Anthropic cache TTL: 5 min (1.25x write) or 1 hour (2x write) | Measurement question: the vase chat's 6-minute pause rewrote everything (13–21% of all cache writes in that run) | new from M2 gap 5 | **decided 2026-10-29: 5 min for now.** Revisit with phase 2 numbers (how often a chat pauses longer than 5 min). |
| D8 | `prompt_cache_key` per chat on OpenAI | Add it (project + chat id); without it all JusPrin users hash to the same machines and overflow above ~15 req/min | new from M2 gap 4; cheap, no behaviour change | **decided 2026-10-29: add it** (project + chat id); part of R8 |
| D9 | Write cost of a larger chat record | Never measured (searched git, memory, 1,055 Claude and 637 Codex sessions; every timing is for mesh/3MF saves). Closed

... [7841 characters truncated] ...

ired skills in the record on both providers as operator-role in-conversation messages; `clear_at: "next_user_message"` on Anthropic, visible and short on OpenAI; stop dropping them from the next OpenAI request | guard; evals (model-visible) | not started |
| R3a Remove the 64 KiB rolling trim and the 16 KiB result cut (neither did anything measured) | D3 decided | session started 2026-10-29 (with R1) |
| R3b Visible compaction at the real context limit: a chat item the person sees, earlier items' lifetime cleared, record untouched, new cache knowingly | D3 decided; needs R7's record | not started, after R7 |
| R4 Keep earlier messages' workspace blocks in the record (user role, as sent) | guard | not started |
| R5 Keep pictures in the record (blob references; ~1,050 Anthropic tokens each) | guard | not started |
| R6 Project-chat notes move from user-text prefix to the operator role (Anthropic in-array `system`, OpenAI `developer`); printer chat's developer notes unchanged in role; kept in the record, never cleared | D2 decided; evals (model-visible); gateway pass-through check | not started |
| R7 Store each turn as sent, thinking included; delete the prototype's carry mechanism, keep its test; un-hide the `[history-prefix]` cases (drop the `[.]` tag) so CTest runs them; refuse a cross-wire-format model switch on an existing chat (D5) | D1, D5 decided, D9 closed; gateway pass-through check first | not started |
| R8 Cache hygiene from M2 gaps: skill breakpoint placement, `prompt_cache_key` (D8), always offer `object_import` so the tool list never changes (tools come first on Anthropic; any change voids the cache), 5-min TTL stays (D7) | D8 decided | session started 2026-10-29 |

| L0 Request-body logging in the shell harness (every body as posted, per request, on disk) | nothing | session started 2026-10-29 |

Prerequisites for any model-visible step (R2, R6, R7): request-body logging in the shell harness, then baselines: OpenAI journeys (none exist) and the prompt-case set on its last confirmed model.

## Phase 2: live confirmation (paid, needs D6)

One three-chat batch on Anthropic and one on OpenAI, before and after. Opus baseline exists in
`.claude/worktrees/opus-cost-batch/opus-batch/out-baseline/`. Measure cache reads vs cache
writes from the usage fields, plus answer quality via the eval harness. Add request-body logging
to the harness first (see M4) so the "after" run can be checked body by body, not only by tokens.

## Branches and worktrees

| Branch | Worktree | Holds |
|---|---|---|
| `claude/cache-invariant-test-51dab5` | `.claude/worktrees/cache-invariant-test-51dab5` | guard test commit; untracked `cache-rules.md` |
| `claude/tool-record-terminal-0b61d2` | `.claude/worktrees/tool-record-terminal-0b61d2` | M3 fix commit |
| `claude/opus-cost-batch` | `.claude/worktrees/opus-cost-batch` | uncommitted prototype + Anthropic harness switch; batch logs under `opus-batch/` |
| `claude/chat-history-cache` | `.claude/worktrees/chat-history-cache` | integration branch: guard test + M3 fix + MCP bridge fix merged (`cd4162fa97`); phase 1 reverts land here |

## Side issue: 7 "MCP bridge" agent tests hang on HEAD

Found by M2 and M3 independently; unrelated to this work. The bridge's check that JusPrin is running never gets an answer from the in-process app server (`test_mcp_bridge.cpp:120`). The M3 session started a session of its own to look into it (`fix-mcp-bridge-tests-pro`, `local_45c7b710-9040-42f0-8e55-0b7952f1e540`); Kenneth did not ask for that one. Outcome: fixed in `8f18a22dc8` on `claude/dreamy-ramanujan-fcaede` (5-line change to `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Mcp/Bridge/CMakeLists.txt`): `c177a160b3` left the bridge library compiled with a different Boost.Asio setting than the rest of the test binary. Merged onto `claude/chat-history-cache` at Kenneth's request (2026-10-29).

## Log

- 2026-10-29: plan approved by Kenneth; M1, M2, M3 started as sessions on Opus 5.5.
- 2026-10-29: M1, M2, M3 done. Added D7, D8, R0, R8 from their findings. Nothing merged or pushed.
- 2026-10-29: R0 done on `claude/chat-history-cache` (guard, M3 fix, MCP bridge fix). D9 closed, M5 skipped. Open: D1–D8.
- 2026-10-29: Kenneth approved the roles-and-lifetimes design in side session `local_97f342dd`. D1 and D2 decided, D4 narrowed to two choices. R1, R2, R6, R8 reworded; the eval-baseline prerequisite added. Open: D3, D4 (pick), D5 (pointer), D6, D7, D8. Nothing merged or pushed.
- 2026-10-29: Kenneth settled D3 (visible compaction), D4 (delete), D6 (approved), D7 (5 min), D8 (add). R3 split into R3a (deletion now) and R3b (compaction, after R7). L0 added. Three sessions started on Opus 5.5: L0, R1+R3a, R8.
- 2026-10-29: D5 decided in a forked side session: same-wire-format switching allowed (one cold cache, no history edit); cross-format switch starts a new chat. D4 explained: the reminder is JusPrin's own sentence, file contents never become operator messages. Open: D3, D4 (pick), D6, D7, D8.

name: jusprin-worktree-build
description: How to configure a JusPrin worktree build reusing existing deps; BUILD_TESTS=ON needed for tests
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 01c34c35-1546-40fb-a600-c49b2e1ffa06
  modified: 2026-09-18T23:36:14.653Z
---

A JusPrin git worktree builds against the already-built deps by configuring:

```
cmake -B build/arm64 -G "Ninja Multi-Config" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local;/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local" \
  -DSLIC3R_GUI=ON -DSLIC3R_STATIC=ON -DSLIC3R_PCH=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=ON \
  -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib
```

CMAKE BINARY (2026-09-29): configure with `/Applications/CMake.app/Contents/bin/cmake` (put it first on PATH). Homebrew's cmake 4.1 at /opt/homebrew/bin fails with "Could NOT find Eigen3 (missing: EIGEN3_VERSION_OK) (Required is at least version 5.0.1)", and a failed configure poisons the cache: `rm -rf build` before retrying.

The two `CMAKE_AR`/`CMAKE_RANLIB` flags are required on a FRESH build dir:
without them Apple's ar is used and liblibslic3r_gui.a (>4 GiB in
RelWithDebInfo) fails to archive. They only work at first configure, not on
reconfigure. Full story: agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md. See
[[liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit]].

FRESH WORKTREE TRAP (2026-09-18): building only `shell_integration_harness`
does not build the web pages. Also build `--target jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs`
(needs node on PATH: /Users/kenneth/.nvm/versions/node/v24.13.0/bin). Without
them resources/jusprin/{home,agent}/index.html are missing, no web views are
created, and the harness silently tests something else (printer panel starts
shown; web-view crashes vanish).

`BUILD_TESTS=ON` is required or the tests/ tree (workspace, shell targets) is
not generated. Build with `cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo
--target <targets>`. wxWidgets 3.3 sources for API verification live under
/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/dep_wxWidgets-prefix/.

CWD TRAP (cost real time once): the harness resets the Bash cwd to the main
repo /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin between turns, so a *relative*
`cmake --build build/arm64` silently builds the MAIN repo's build dir, not the
worktree's — the worktree binary then runs stale code and a re-fix looks like it
"didn't take". Always pass the worktree build dir as an ABSOLUTE path to
`cmake --build /…/.claude/worktrees/<wt>/build/arm64 …`, and run test binaries by
absolute path. Also: `cmake --build --target <one_exe>` may relink against a
stale lib without recompiling a changed .cpp in that lib — build the app target
(e.g. OrcaSlicer) too so the lib recompiles; verify with
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' build.log`. Editing tools (Edit/Write) use absolute
paths so source edits land correctly regardless of cwd.

STALE PROMPT TRAP (2026-09-23): `--target shell_integration_harness` does NOT
rebuild the web pages, so a harness run after an edit to AgentUI (for example
printerInstructions.ts) loads the old bundle. Six --printer-live runs were

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""prefix_check.py on hand-written bodies and a hand-written log directory.

Usage: python3 tests/project_prompt/test_prefix_check.py
"""

import contextlib
import importlib.util
import io
import json
import pathlib
import tempfile
import unittest

HERE = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent
spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("prefix_check", HERE / "prefix_check.py")
prefix_check = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
spec.loader.exec_module(prefix_check)

FIRST = b'{"model":"m","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}],"stream":true}'
GROWN = b'{"model":"m","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"},{"role":"assistant","content":"yo"}],"stream":true}'
EDITED = b'{"model":"m","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hey"},{"role":"assistant","content":"yo"}],"stream":true}'


class CompareTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_a_grown_chat_is_an_append(self):
        result = prefix_check.compare(FIRST, GROWN)
        self.assertEqual(result["kind"], "append")
        self.assertEqual(result["common_prefix"], FIRST.index(b"],"))
        self.assertEqual(result["earlier_path"], "$.messages")
        self.assertEqual(result["later_path"], "$.messages")

    def test_an_edited_message_is_named_by_its_path(self):
        result = prefix_check.compare(FIRST, EDITED)
        self.assertEqual(result["kind"], "changed")
        self.assertEqual(result["first_difference"], FIRST.index(b'hi"') + 1)
        self.assertEqual(result["earlier_path"], "$.messages[0].content")
        self.assertEqual(result["later_path"], "$.messages[0].content")

    def test_a_key_byte_belongs_to_its_member(self):
        earlier = b'{"a":[1,{"name":"x"}]}'
        later = b'{"a":[1,{"nome":"x"}]}'
        result = prefix_check.compare(earlier, later)
        self.assertEqual(result["earlier_path"], "$.a[1].name")
        self.assertEqual(result["later_path"], "$.a[1].nome")

    def test_odd_keys_are_quoted(self):
        self.assertEqual(prefix_check.path_text(["input", 3, "a-b"]), '$.input[3]["a-b"]')

    def test_identical_bodies(self):
        result = prefix_check.compare(FIRST, FIRST)
        self.assertEqual(result["kind"], "identical")
        self.assertEqual(result["common_prefix"], len(FIRST))


class LogTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def write(self, directory, n, body, chat, purpose="reply"):
        (directory / ("%04d-request.json" % n)).write_bytes(body)
        (directory / ("%04d-request.meta.json" % n)).write_text(json.dumps({"chat_id": chat, "purpose": purpose}))

    def test_pairs_are_consecutive_requests_of_one_chat_and_purpose(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as name:
            directory = pathlib.Path(name)
            self.write(directory, 1, FIRST, "c1")
            self.write(directory, 2, b'{"input":"title"}', "c1", "title")
            self.write(directory, 3, FIRST, "c2")
            self.write(directory, 4, GROWN, "c1")
            self.write(directory, 5, EDITED, "c2")
            pairs = prefix_check.check(directory)
        self.assertEqual([(p["chat_id"], p["earlier"], p["later"], p["kind"]) for p in pairs],
                         [("c1", "0001", "0004", "append"), ("c2", "0003", "0005", "changed")])

    def test_an_ignored_key_is_left_out_of_both(self):
        earlier = b'{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"hi","cache_control":{"type":"ephemeral"}}]}]}'
        later = (b'{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"hi"}]},'
                 b'{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"more","cache_control":{"type":"ephemeral"}}]}]}')
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as name:
            directory = pathlib.Path(name)
            self.write(directory, 1, earlier, "c1")
            self.write(directory, 2, later, "c1")
            self.assertEqual(prefix_check.check(directory)[0]["earlier_path"], "$.messages[0].content[0]")
            self.assertEqual(prefix_check.check(directory, ["cache_control"])[0]["kind"], "append")
            out = io.StringIO()
            with contextlib.redirect_stdout(out):
                prefix_check.main([name, "--ignore-key", "cache_control"])
        self.assertIn("[append]", out.getvalue())
        self.assertIn("as rewritten, not as posted", out.getvalue())


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()
EOF

## What keeps it faithful to the app

- **The system prompt** comes from the page's own source, through
  `tests/printer_prompt/render_prompt.mjs` (`"kind": "project"`) and the page's
  esbuild. This needs node and the AgentUI npm install. `--prompt-rev REV`
  renders it as it was at a git revision, 6b4b8b6188 or later (the commit
  that moved the prompt from C++ to the page, unchanged).
- **`project_tools.json`** is the tool list the app sends in the project chat
  with nothing attached. `test_openai_responses_agent.cpp` fails when it
  drifts from the registry. Regenerate it with
  `JUSPRIN_UPDATE_PROJECT_TOOLS=1 agent_bridge_tests '[project]'`.
- **Everything else in the request** is the app's: `requests.json`, recorded
  by the shell harness from `script.json`:

  ```bash
  build/arm64/tests/shell/Release/JusPrinShellHarness.app/Contents/MacOS/JusPrinShellHarness \
      --project-prompt-requests tests/project_prompt/script.json tests/project_prompt/requests.json
  ```

  The harness runs the real app on its two-plate fixture (Bambu Lab X1 Carbon
  0.4, Bambu PLA Basic, 0.20mm Standard, plate 1 sliced) with the project
  chat's real OpenAI adapter, but the adapter's requests go nowhere: each is
  answered with the next model output the script gives. The tools run for
  real, and the app builds every request itself: the earlier turns as
  `AgentHost::make_agent_request` replays them (calls with their results, a
  result over 16 KiB replaced by the omission note, at most 20 entries), the
  new message as `OpenAIResponsesAgent::initial_input` builds it (the
  person's words, then the app's `<print_issue>` and `<workspace>` blocks,
  each a part of its own), a canvas issue's message and context, a file-load report and its
  developer line, the file-loaded skill and the plate's picture on the
  request that first carries a load report, the print-issues skill on the
  request that carries a chip's message or first shows a slice's new
  warnings, the slice-failed skill on the request that first shows a
  refused or failed slice, the setup skill on the request that first
  carries a recorded or changed purpose or a setup change under one, and
  the live results of this turn's calls with the
  workspace block `AgentHost::continue_after_tool` adds. Arguments that need
  ids take them from the real previous result (`{{result/sessionId}}`) or the
  project (`{{workspace/activePlateId}}`). For each request it keeps, the
  harness checks the tools equal `project_tools.json` and the instructions
  equal `projectInstructions.fixture.txt`, then leaves both out of the file;
  the runner puts the rendered prompt and `project_tools.json` back. The
  script's `answers` list names the reads recorded at every point.
  `test_openai_responses_agent.cpp` also checks every recorded result and
  answer against its tool's output schema.
- **Answered reads** are added as the app continues a turn: the model's own
  output items, then a result for every call under its call id, in the order
  the calls were written. Each answer carries the action id and workspace
  block of the recorded call. A point's `once` (in `requests.json`) counts
  the last items of its request that the app sends on that request alone,
  a skill's text and, for the file-loaded skill, its picture; the runner
  drops them before it answers
  a read, as the app does.
- **Skills** (`AgentUI/src/skills/*/SKILL.md`) reach the model only in the
  recorded requests: the app adds one to the request where its event first
  reaches the model, as that request's last item. The recorder checks that a
  point the script marks `"skill": "<name>"` ends with that skill (after the
  plate's picture for `file-loaded`), that no other point
  carries a skill or a picture, so an import's point carries the
  file-loaded skill alone, and that the next request of the same turn (the
  first answered read) has none.

## Running it

The runner and `test_steps.py` need the app's argument check built:
`cmake --build <build dir> --config <config> --target tool_call_check`. The
runner takes the newest one under `build/` (or `JUSPRIN_TOOL_CALL_CHECK`) and
stops when it is older than `ToolRegistry.cpp`.

By default every case runs 3 times (`RUN_BUDGET` 78 shared by the cases run,
at most 20 for one case alone); `--runs N` sets it. `--verbose` prints every
run's conversation. Usage is logged for every response on stderr and totalled
at the end.

A run ends with every case it ran beside the baseline (below). It exits 1
when a case is marked worse, 0 otherwise; `--must-pass N` makes the exit code
1 when a case passes fewer than N runs instead, as before baselines.
`--results FILE` also saves the run's counts in the baseline's form, and
`--compare FILE` prints a saved run beside the baseline again without sending
anything.

```bash
tests/project_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py --render-only --prompt-rev 6b4b8b6188 > bodies.jsonl
```

prints every request body it would send and their sizes, and sends nothing.

All runs of all the cases run share one pool of `--jobs` workers (5 by
default, 3 for the claude-cli backend below), and each run's line gives its
wall-clock time.

## Request bodies as posted (`--request-log`)

`requests.json` holds bodies for this suite to send, with stored results cut
to 4,000 characters. To see what the app itself posts, byte for byte, give
the shell harness `--request-log <directory>` beside `--live-agent`,
`--manual-live-agent` or `--project-prompt-requests`. The directory must be
new or empty. For the n-th request of the run it writes:

- `NNNN-request.json`: the body exactly as the transport was given it.
- `NNNN-request.meta.json`: provider, URL, header names (credential values
  redacted), chat id, purpose (`reply` or `title`), request id, attempt, time
  and body length.
- `NNNN-response.sse`: the response stream as received.
- `NNNN-response.json`: outcome, HTTP status, usage as the provider named its
  fields, stop reason, the assembled text and any error.

```bash
build/arm64/tests/shell/Release/JusPrinShellHarness.app/Contents/MacOS/JusPrinShellHarness \
    --project-prompt-requests tests/project_prompt/script.json /tmp/requests.json --request-log /tmp/request-log
```

The scripted run sends nothing and its responses carry no usage. Only the
project chat's Agent is logged: the printer panel builds its own from the app
configuration, and so does the host when a chat picks a model other than the
one the harness installed. `tests/jusprin_support/RequestLog.hpp` wraps any
transport and agent, so another harness mode can log the same way.

`prefix_check.py` then compares each request with the one before it of the
same chat and purpose: the common byte prefix, the first byte that differs and
the JSON path it belongs to in each body. A provider caches a prompt prefix,
so a difference inside an earlier message is a cache leak; `[append]` means the
earlier body ended an array where the later one goes on with it.

```bash
python3 tests/project_prompt/prefix_check.py /tmp/request-log
python3 tests/project_prompt/prefix_check.py /tmp/request-log --ignore-key cache_control --json
```

`--ignore-key cache_control` leaves out Anthropic's moving breakpoint, which
differs on every request without changing what is cached; the bodies are then
compared as Python writes them back, not as posted. `test_prefix_check.py`
checks it on hand-written bodies.
